title: Pasco Resists-Honor Veterans on D-Day

location.venue: Intersection of Little Rd and Citizens Dr

description:
On D-Day Anniversary, Pasco Resists Honors Veterans and Demands Protection of the VA

New Port Richey, FL — On the 81st anniversary of D-Day, Pasco Resists honors the sacrifice, bravery, and patriotism of American service members who fought on the beaches of Normandy to defend democracy and defeat fascism. A protest will take place on Friday June 6th from 4-6pm at the West Government Pasco Center, the intersection of Little Rd and Citizens Dr, (8731 Citizens Dr.)

“June 6 is a sacred date in our shared history,” said Doris Carroll, advocate, and leader with Pasco Resists. “It marks the moment when ordinary Americans did something extraordinary —risking everything to protect freedom not just for our nation, but for the world.”

The D-Day anniversary comes at a time when veterans face new battles at home. From underfunded healthcare to attempts to privatize and dismantle the VA, many veterans struggle to get the support they deserve after their service.

“Honoring our veterans means more than speeches—it means action,” said Carroll. “It means protecting the VA, expanding mental health care, and making sure no veteran is left behind.”

Pasco Resists is calling on elected officials and the public to recommit policies that truly honor the legacy of those who served. That includes rejecting VA budget cuts, improving access to healthcare, housing, and job opportunities, and standing against extremism in all forms.

“The men and women of D-Day didn’t fight to see their legacy used as a political prop,” Carroll added. “They fought for freedom, for equality, and for a better future. That’s the legacy we must live up to.”
________________________________________
About Pasco Resists
Pasco Resists is a grassroots organization based in Pasco County, Florida. We are dedicated to defending and uplifting veterans and working families through advocacy, education, and direct action. We believe a just society is one where every veteran receives the care, respect, and support they have earned.

title: An Evening with Former NC Rep. John Autry

location.venue: Special Events & Education Center @ Atrium Health Stanly

description:
## Hope in Times of Hopelessness

Former Representative John Autry of the North Carolina House will visit Albemarle to share reflections on his years of public service, what motivates him, and why it matters now more than ever. Most importantly, he’ll offer a call to action: whether it's a seat on the school board or in the state legislature.

### Join Indivisible Uwharrie and the Stanly County Democratic Women for this special evening of inspiration and engagement.

On December 31, 2024, John Autry retired from the North Carolina House of Representatives, concluding his service representing District 100 in Mecklenburg County.

Born and raised in Fayetteville, Autry graduated from Pine Forest High School in 1971 before moving to California to attend college. His studies were interrupted when he enlisted in the U.S. Navy, where he served honorably from 1972 to 1976 and was discharged with the rank of Petty Officer Third Class (E-4). After his military service, he returned to California State University, Fullerton, to complete his education.

Autry pursued a career in film production and returned to North Carolina in 1981 during a boom in the local film industry. Settling in Charlotte, he enjoyed a career spanning over 27 years as a cameraman, editor, producer, and director. In 1999, he directed a series of public service announcements for the local NBC affiliate. One of those spots, Tea Party, won the national Emmy Award for Best PSA of the Year.

After finishing second in the 2006 Democratic primary for U.S. Congress (NC-08), Autry was recruited to run for the Mecklenburg Soil & Water Conservation District Board of Supervisors, where he was re-elected in 2010. When the long-time incumbent for Charlotte City Council District 5 chose not to seek re-election, Autry was encouraged to run. He was elected in 2011 and re-elected twice before successfully running for the open seat in North Carolina House District 100, where he served four terms.

John Autry is married to Rebecca Wyndham. Together, they have four children and six grandchildren. John says being a grandparent is the one thing in life that truly isn’t overrated. Those six grandchildren, and the world he hopes to help shape for them, remain his greatest motivation for public service.

IN PERSON!!! DREAM Mayoral Zine making Party/Postcarding to voters!!!

Come and join your neighbors from local & neighboring communities for an in-person DREAM Mayoral Zine making Party & postcard writing event! 

Make new friends and discuss local and national issues, all while saving democracy by writing postcards to voters and getting the DREAM out by making ZINES! 

We will provide all you will need, including zine templates, postcards, stamps, voter addresses, and maybe some snacks! Just bring yourself, a few friends and your best handwriting!

If you like, feel free to bring any of the following:

Snacks or Beverages to share, Postcard Stamps, Colorful Pens & Markers, and stickers for decorating!

New York City doesn’t need to replace one power-hungry, scandal-ridden politician with another. We can elect a mayor we can all be proud of, but we must do it together! With multiple progressive candidates running, we are taking on the challenge of keeping progressives united, instead of splitting our base of voters.

This year is not about crawling into our corners — it’s about using ranked choice voting to consolidate the power of our collective vote. That’s why we’re asking voters to rank ALL candidates on the DREAM Slate to make sure that a progressive champion is the next mayor of New York City.

Postcards to Voters are friendly, handwritten reminders from volunteers to targeted voters giving Democrats a winning edge in close, key races coast to coast. You can help save democracy by encouraging voters to get to the polls to vote for Democratic candidates in battleground areas, notifying voters about special elections, and educating voters on how to make a plan to vote.

title: NO KINGS! "We the People" Democracy Fair in Palo Alto
description:
This Flag Day, join us for a democracy fair. Following a day of peaceful protests held in counterpoint to Donald Trump’s militaristic charade, we will host a celebration of what makes America truly great—and truly good.

On June 14, we will gather not just in protest, but in defiance—loud, proud, joyful defiance of a tinpot wannabe tyrant who thinks that celebrating his birthday matters more than honoring the flag that symbolizes our freedom. The democracy fair will be an occasion for people to convene after No Kings events being held across the Peninsula.

It will be an active, participatory gathering that includes something for everyone: an exhibit of pro-democracy art, music and theatrical performances on the theme of “No Kings,” tables where people can learn about activism opportunities, a Resistance Lab workshop, a costume competition (Elon Musk isn’t welcome, but Elon look-alikes might get a prize), and much more.

This event—jointly sponsored by Bend the Arc, Indivisible Mid-Peninsula, Indivisible Palo Alto Plus, Indivisible Portola Valley, and It’s Blue Turn—will celebrate patriotism, not militarism. In saying NO to kings, we will also say YES to democracy.

The democracy fair will take place at Rinconada Park, and will follow a parade that starts at 2 p.m. The parade will begin at the intersection of El Camino Real and Embarcadero Road. (We invite participants to join us at any point along the 1.5-mile route.) Please sign up for that event as well: https://www.mobilize.us/itsblueturn/event/794490/

title: D Day for Democracy!
description:
June 7 – We Remember. We Resist.

On D-Day, thousands risked and gave their lives to stop the rise of fascism and defend democracy. Today, that fight is not just history—it’s a warning.

We rally on June 7 to say: No Kings. No Tyrants. No Authoritarian Rule. Not then. Not now. Not ever.

As extremist politicians consolidate power, attack our freedoms, and undermine the very foundations of democracy, we are showing up to protect what so many died to preserve.

This is a protest. A rally. A stand for freedom.

Bring a friend. Bring a sign. Bring your voice. June 7 – We defend democracy by using it.

Peoria50501 is a branch of the 50501 Movement, a grassroots national effort made up of everyday Americans from all walks of life who stand for democracy, and who stand against the authoritarian actions of the Trump Administration and an all-too compliant Congress. We are a peaceful, nonviolent, resistance movement, calling on our government to uphold the Constitution and end Executive overreach. We are of, by, and for the people!

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*
